inputs.text:
Well, folks, here we go again. While the political elites jet off to Paris for high-level photo ops with OECD Secretary-General Mathias Cormann and President Luis Abinader on 25 March 2026, they expect the hardworking citizens back home to just swallow their grandstanding. 

Foreign Minister Roberto Álvarez went ahead and signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) to supposedly design the country’s first National Integrity and Anti-Corruption Strategy. But let’s call it what it really is: just another top-down technocratic exercise dictated by global financial elites, rather than a genuine reckoning with structural issues, and an insult to our national sovereignty and traditional values. 

The ruling class simply loves to cozy up to international organizations in France to preach transparency and virtue-signal to Socialist-leaning globalists, turning their backs on personal responsibility and basic social order. But true institutional reform will never, ever come from these corporate-aligned summits while ordinary citizens continue to face economic insecurity and daily challenges on the ground. They are completely out of touch with the traditional values and hard realities of our people, preferring the comfort of foreign capitals over true national accountability and family values.
